title: Assurance labeling and rollout authorization handoff for model releases
creator: Claire Zhang
description:
Problem: We lack a consistent, auditable way to attach assurance evidence and approval metadata to model rollouts. That causes confusion during incident retros, slows down cross-functional sign-offs, and makes automated rollback policies brittle because they lack provenance about who approved what and why.

Goal: Ship an "assurance labeling and authorization handoff" capability in the Console + control plane that: (1) lets PMs/Legal/Security attach structured assurance labels (privacy, safety, perf, legal) and short evidence bundles to a rollout; (2) enforces RBAC-controlled sign-off gates (required signatories per label/profile); (3) records tamper-evident audit events and artifacts to the customer-managed audit log with retention and export; (4) surfaces approval state in the rollout API so runtime and autoscaler can respect policy during canary/A-B/shadow flows; (5) integrates with auto-rollback triggers (quality/regression alerts) tied to the sign-off provenance.

Out of scope for initial iteration: full delegated approval tree UI for entitlements (we will provide a flat required-signers list and an API-driven escalation path).

Success metrics: reduction in manual approval OOO time, fewer post-rollout incidents attributed to missing reviews, and ability to run certified rollouts with automated deny/rollback when required approvals are absent.
acceptance_criteria: Console: ability to add one or more assurance labels to a rollout draft and attach 1-3 evidence links or uploaded PDFs
Control plane API: rollout object exposes 'assurance_labels' and 'approval_state' fields; API returns 403 when initiating final rollout if required approvals absent
RBAC: policy accepts rules like 'role:security -> can_sign:safety' and enforced for UI and API calls
Audit log: each approval/revocation recorded as an append-only event with user, timestamp, label, comment and links to evidence; exportable as newline-delimited JSON
Integration: auto-rollback pipeline consumes approval_state and will block or rollback canary to previous stable model when required approvals are revoked or missing
E2E test: a canary rollout with missing 'privacy' approval is rejected by API; once approved, rollout proceeds and audit entry visible in console and log export
